title: Report on the epidemiological situation of dengue in the Americas (As of epidemiological week 21, 2026. Update: Jun 17 2026 3:24PM (GTM-5))
snippet: In the epidemiological week (EW) 21 of 2026, a total of 1,169,325 suspected cases of dengue were reported, resulting in a cumulative incidence of 113 cases por 100,000 population. This represents a decrease of 64% compared to the same period in 2025 and 69% compared to the average of the last 5 years. Figure 1 shows the trend of suspected dengue cases as of EW 21. [...] Out of the 1,169,325 reported dengue cases in the Region, 318,511 cases (27%) were laboratory-confirmed, and 2,202 (0.2%) were classified as severe dengue. A total of 289 deaths have been recorded, resulting in a case fatality rate (CFR) of 0.025%. 14 countries and territories within the region reported dengue cases in epidemiological week (EW) 21, accounting for 37,388 new suspected cases. Of these, 64 were classified as severe dengue (0.1%), and 6 deaths reported, yielding a case fatality [...] a case fatality rate of 0.016%. title: National Dengue Review 2026 identifies priorities to strengthen Sri Lanka's dengue preparedness and response
snippet:
The current dengue outbreak underscores the continuing public health threat posed by dengue in Sri Lanka. By early August 2026, the country had reported more than 90,000 dengue cases and over 65 dengue-related deaths, making this one of the most significant outbreaks in recent years and placing 2026 on track to become the largest dengue outbreak since the record epidemic of 2017. [...] Caption: A participant at the National Dengue Review analysing data on dengue surveillance and control activities conducted from Jan to Jul -2026, including insecticide susceptibility and double net trap efficacy. (Credit – Sejani Wilegoda / WHO)

### Investing in data, innovation and forecasting

As dengue outbreaks become increasingly influenced by environmental and climatic factors, the use of data and predictive analytics is becoming more important for planning and response. title: WHO Region of the Americas records highest number of dengue cases in history; cases spike in other regions
snippet:
Recent data published by the Pan American Health Organization, which also serves as the WHO Regional Office for the Americas, show that countries reported more than 2.7 million cases and 1206 deaths from January to October 2019, of which over 1.2 million were laboratory-confirmed and more than 22 000 were classified as severe dengue.
